caste.note: Cultures whose names carry caste or trade-guild forms: buildings, events, inns, money, settlement context and streets each kept this pair.

dutchAmerican.note: Money: the cultures whose coin names read the Dutch and American shapes.

britainSource.note: Bynames: cultures that draw their forenames from the British source. Differs from the `british` group: it includes general.

noPlaceNames.note: Peoples and tongues, bynames: cultures with no place-name form.

realmsChristian.note: Realms' own Christian set. Differs from the vocabulary's `christian` group (it includes general and ethiopian): kept as it is.

plainNicknames.note: Named things: cultures whose nickname forms aren't reduced.

routesGods.note: Route names: cultures with god-named routes.

festivalsAncient.note: Time and sky: cultures whose ancient calendars carry festivals.

seasonPairNorth.note: Time and sky: cultures reading a two-season pair from the ancient era to the medieval.

seasonPairMeso.note: Time and sky: cultures reading a season pair from the ancient era to the early modern; also the Mesoamerican calendar round.

elementsEastAsian.note: Time and sky: cultures whose week-7 system reads the five elements.

vesselRealmCultures.note: Vessels: the cultures a realm short form can be drawn for (the realms roster); others read general.

notes.aircraft: Read from docs/aircraft-and-land-vehicles-brief.md §4.1 (the data's `technology` carries labels, not dates): A1 balloons and kites (kites from antiquity, balloons from 1783) AN–ST; A2 airships (1852 to the 1930s) ST, MO; A3 pioneer and biplane (1903 to the 1920s) ST, MO; A4 piston age, A5 jet age and A6 modern and drones MO; A7 future NF, IS; AF sky ships, fantastic only: the eras of the settings that offer it (FH is MD, MF is MO, §4.3).
notes.landVehicles: Read from docs/aircraft-and-land-vehicles-brief.md §4.2: L1 animal-drawn (chariots to coaches, in use throughout) AN–ST; L2 steam ST; L3 early motor (cars from the 1880s, the first tanks, electric trams) ST, MO; L4 mid-century and L5 modern MO; L6 future NF, IS; LF war engines and wonders, fantastic only: MD (FH) and MO (MF).

shares.$comment: Northern Europe brief 5a §11.3, 5b §12.1 and brief 6a §9.3: `signature` is the share of a module's own-shape draws that a core-depth culture's signature entries take (every core culture and every second-tier culture whose batch is done); `signatureMix` is the Celtic-style share the mixes (Celtic, Iberian, Greek and Byzantine) take; `region` is what region-weighted shapes take when a region is chosen.

module.$comment: Sibling-distinctness brief: a floor under the share of a module's draws that a core-depth culture's own entries take, for modules whose general draw would otherwise leave a culture within reach of General (a calendar, the sky, arms: names that carry no people).

legacy.$comment: Sibling-distinctness brief (17 November 2026): a culture that reads a table it shares with a sibling (the nations read Celtic, Scandinavian reads Norse, Spanish and Portuguese read Iberian, Greek and Byzantine read Greek-and-Byzantine, Anglo-Saxon and Norman and British read the English tables) draws that shared table at this weight, the share of its own-shape draws that are not its own entries; its own entries take the rest. Lower it until the pair meets the limits in the distinctness section.

regionExempt.$comment: Northern Europe brief 5b §12.2: regions that do not have a module's landscape. Their cells are exempt from the six-entry region depth, and a chosen region there falls back to the culture's own draws.

sourceShares.$comment: Place modules split brief §4.1: where a focused place module's draw comes from, before it falls back to its own shapes. A kind may list sources; the share is the chance a draw tries the source first.

cultureRegions.$comment: Northern Europe brief §3.1, §4: the regions each module culture key reads, where the region link shows, its default and how it reads. `fixed`: one region, drawn as plain text; `all`: the link also offers the whole culture. Modules in a batch use the `regions` group; the rest keep `british`.

engineAlias.$comment: Northern Europe brief §3: the module culture keys that came after the legacy ones read the legacy key's plumbing (settlement names, people lists, realms, gods, the colonial link and the weight tables) wherever a table has no row of their own.
engineAlias.$ownTablesComment: Brief 6a: a key that has tables of its own in some modules (French, Dutch and Iberian money, vessels and the settlement vocabulary) reads them there and its alias elsewhere; `engineOwn` lists those modules.

deferred.$comment: Brief 6a §9.6: cells the styles brief owns. A culture of the batch in one of these modules is reported as deferred, not below target.

distinctness.$comment: Sibling-distinctness brief (17 November 2026), docs/second-tier-tables-brief.md section 10. tests/distinctness.test.ts runs every module at its default state, only the culture changed, over `seeds`, `count` names each; a pair's overlap is the share of A's names that B also gives at the same seed. `siblings` are held to `siblingLimit` percent, each of `general` against General to `generalLimit`. Not measured: `excludedModules` (deferred styles, and deserts, which have no landscape of their own in these lands), `excludedCells` (module and culture), the settlement kit, and a mix against its own halves. A later batch adds its sibling pairs and its cultures to `general` here, and must pass.
distinctness.$pairComment: Second pass (18 November 2026, §12 of the second-tier brief): every pair of distinct cultures in `general`, siblings or not, shares at most `pairLimit` percent in every measured module; listed siblings keep `siblingLimit`.
